articles.authors: Zilin Wang · Binghui Li · Jia-Nan Wang · Lean Wang · Jinbo Wang · Lei Wu
articles.title: Noise turns the sign discontinuity into a local slope
articles.evidence: Read §2–3 and §6.1; acceptance was previously reported by the author, and this is the first arXiv version

blocks.text: Let g be one coordinate of the true gradient, a its single-sample noise standard deviation, and B the batch size. Under the Gaussian noise surrogate, mean sign responds nearly linearly when the gradient is small relative to batch noise. [1]

blocks.label: Scalar expansion from §6.1; the response saturates for large signals
With diagonal features and curvature-aligned noise variance, the local drift has square-root curvature

blocks.tex: \mathbb E[\mathcal E_t]\asymp S(t)+\int_0^tK(t-\tau)n_B(\tau)\,d\tau,\qquad S(t)\asymp t^{-2s},\quad K(t)\asymp t^{-(2-2/q)}
blocks.label: Theorem 3.1: intrinsic time t; s and q come from the source and spectral-decay conditions; n_B is noise injection

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Signal error decays faster and noise is forgotten more slowly than for SGD, yielding different comparisons in hard and easy regimes. The theorem concerns a diagonal power-law regression SDE under curvature alignment and stepsize and time conditions. Pretraining results do not establish the same mechanism for matrix Muon. [1]

articles.paper: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling
articles.authors: Jie Ren · Jonathan Rosenfeld · Neil Thompson
articles.title: Start more prefixes and finish fewer paths

blocks.text: PreG samples reasoning prefixes of length k, ranks them by internal confidence, and completes only the top fraction α. Let T be full path length and B the generation-token budget; the expression ignores rounding and variable path lengths. [2]

blocks.tex: B=M_{\rm pre}k+M_{\rm comp}(T-k),\quad M_{\rm comp}=\alpha M_{\rm pre}=\frac{\alpha B}{k+\alpha(T-k)}
blocks.label: A smaller α filters more aggressively but reduces the number of completed paths
Proposition 1 approximation for independent bounded path margins with mean μ and variance σ²; explains aggregation without asserting independence after ranking

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Screening is most useful near the decision boundary, but a single rule does not improve every benchmark. This is inference-time answer selection: dropping low-confidence prefixes changes the sampling distribution and provides no unbiased policy-gradient estimator. [2]

articles.title: The local rate comes from linearization
articles.evidence: Read Definitions 1.1 and 2.2–2.3, Theorem 1.2 and Lemma 2.7

blocks.text: The normalization denominator has a positive offset b₀,₁. As momentum vanishes, finitely many odd polynomial steps act locally like scalar multiplication. This is different from exact polar flattening of all nonzero singular values. [3]

blocks.label: First-order term from Lemma 2.7; the positive coefficient is absorbed into the effective stepsize
Optimal local χ-rate of Theorem 1.2, with χ the Hessian condition number at the minimum

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The theorem uses deterministic local analysis, positive definite Hessian and the specified normalization. It does not give the same rate for zero-offset normalization, exact polar or stochastic training far from the minimum, nor establish local acceleration over momentum. [3]

title: Noise preconditioning, prefix screening, and local Muon rates
subtitle: SignSGD · PreG · Muon · classic signSGD
intro: Three readings ask how training noise changes curvature, how inference prefixes allocate generation, and what makes Muon fast locally. The classic revisits one-bit communication and sign errors in signSGD.

classic.title: Distributed optimization as sign voting
classic.paper: signSGD: Compressed Optimisation for Non-Convex Problems
classic.authors: Jeremy Bernstein · Yu-Xiang Wang · Kamyar Azizzadenesheli · Anima Anandkumar
classic.dateNote: First arXiv posting February 12, 2018 ET; read the ICML 2018 version
classic.evidence: Read §2–4; one-step descent and binomial expressions are simplified derivations
classic.question: If worker noise is positively correlated due to shared samples or randomness, what voting error rate remains possible at a fixed marginal wrong-sign rate?

blocks.text: Taking coordinatewise signs lets each worker send one bit per coordinate. Gradient magnitudes are lost, so the analysis controls wrong-sign probabilities rather than reusing an unbiased-SGD proof. [19,20]

blocks.tex: x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta\,\operatorname{sign}(\hat g_k),\quad f(x+d)\le f(x)+g^\top d+\tfrac12\sum_i L_i d_i^2
blocks.label: Algorithm 1 and coordinatewise smoothness; g=∇f(x)
Equivalent identity with binary signs and no ties; a wrong sign reverses descent
One-step bound: nominal descent, wrong-sign penalty, and curvature cost
Simplification for iid workers and odd m; voting suppresses error when qᵢ<1/2

blocks.text: Under a lower bound, coordinatewise smoothness and variance conditions, Theorem 1 takes batch K and stepsize proportional to K⁻¹ᐟ², giving an expected average gradient ℓ₁ norm of O(K⁻¹ᐟ²). This uses K² stochastic gradient calls. The improved voting bound also uses symmetric unimodal noise. [19]
